news.title: Indonesia Nickel Ore Market Weekly ReportIndonesia Nickel Market Nickel ore prices continue to decline, with sharper losses in medium- and high-grade saprolite Indonesian nickel ore prices continued to weaken this week, with medium- and high-grade saprolite recording significantly larger declines than low-grade limonite. According to the weekly market report, the average prices of 1.2% Ni and 1.3% Ni limonite fell to US$25.5/wmt and US$27.5/wmt, respectively, down US$1/wmt from the previous assessment. Meanwhile, 1.4% Ni, 1.5% Ni and 1.6% Ni saprolite declined to US$47.1/wmt, US$52.5/wmt and US$57.1/wmt, representing decreases of US$4.7/wmt, US$6.0/wmt and US$6.3/wmt, respectively. Nickel ore grade Previous price (US$/wmt) Latest price (US$/wmt) Change 1.2% Ni limonite 26.5 25.5 -1.0 1.3% Ni limonite 28.5 27.5 -1.0 1.4% Ni saprolite 51.8 47.1 -4.7 1.5% Ni saprolite 58.5 52.5 -6.0 1.6% Ni saprolite 63.4 57.1 -6.3 The sharper decline in saprolite prices indicates that the market's previous tightness in higher-grade ore has eased, shifting bargaining power further towards buyers. Lower official benchmarks, expectations of additional supply from supplementary RKAB allocations, and cautious smelter purchasing are collectively weighing on spot prices. In the near term, Indonesian nickel ore prices are likely to remain under pressure unless supply growth slows or downstream purchasing improves. October second-half HMA and HPM reductions reinforce bearish sentiment Indonesia's Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) announced the nickel ore benchmark prices for the second half of October 2026. The Harga Mineral Acuan (HMA) declined from US$16,322.67/mt in the first half of October to US$15,847.67/mt in the second half, a decrease of US$475/mt or 2.91%. Nickel grade Previous HPM (US$/wmt) New HPM (US$/wmt) Change 1.2% Ni 23.19 22.44 -0.75 1.3% Ni 46.07 44.58 -1.49 1.4% Ni 51.66 50.05 -1.61 1.5% Ni 56.22 54.48 -1.74 1.6% Ni 61.00 59.12 -1.88 The HMA and HPM reductions establish a lower official pricing reference for domestic nickel ore transactions. Actual transaction prices may still vary according to grade, moisture content, contractual terms, quality adjustments and transportation costs. The lower benchmarks reinforce the downward trend and may influence negotiations between miners and smelters. Market participants will therefore monitor how quickly the revised HPM is reflected in actual transaction prices. Supplementary RKAB allocations could increase fourth-quarter ore supply Indonesia's supplementary 2026 RKAB allocations are being released progressively. Market attention has shifted from quota approvals to whether the additional allocations will translate into actual production and shipments. Newly approved quotas do not immediately create physical supply, as mining companies still need to mobilise equipment, maintain roads, prepare stockpiles and arrange transportation. Nevertheless, as more mines resume or expand production, Indonesian nickel ore availability could increase further in the fourth quarter. If this additional supply enters the market while smelter purchasing remains weak, the imbalance between supply and demand could intensify, putting further pressure on spot ore prices. Smelter inventories remain sufficient, while some RKEF lines operate at reduced rates According to the supplied weekly report, Indonesian smelter feedstock inventories are estimated to cover approximately two months of consumption. Pyrometallurgical operations have reported coverage of around 2.7 months, while hydrometallurgical operations have approximately 1.8 months of coverage. These figures suggest that smelters have limited immediate incentive to replenish inventories aggressively, with spot purchases mainly directed towards meeting production requirements. In addition, some RKEF production lines in Morowali have reportedly been affected by industrial water shortages. Based on the SMM survey information provided, certain lines have operated at approximately 30–40% of normal levels since 22 September. This reduction applies to the affected lines and should not be interpreted as a production rate for the entire industrial park. Lower RKEF operating rates reduce saprolite consumption and can further weaken spot purchasing demand. If water shortages persist, actual ore consumption could fall below previous expectations, particularly while inventories remain sufficient. The combination of additional supply from RKAB allocations and weaker demand from affected smelters therefore represents a significant source of downward pressure on Indonesian nickel ore prices. El Niño and water shortages remain key operational risks Indonesia's principal weather-related concern is prolonged dryness and insufficient industrial water availability, rather than the heavy seasonal rainfall affecting parts of the Philippines. Nickel-producing areas such as Morowali face potential constraints on smelting operations when water supplies become insufficient. The market impact is primarily transmitted through demand. Reduced smelter operating rates lower ore consumption and may cause some facilities to reduce spot purchases. However, the effect on refined nickel prices could differ if production losses become sufficiently large. Monitoring should focus on industrial water availability, operating rates at affected RKEF lines, smelter inventory drawdowns and any confirmed production adjustments. Indonesia outlook: bearish conditions likely to persist Indonesia's nickel ore market is expected to remain weak in the near term. Lower HMA and HPM benchmarks, the gradual release of supplementary RKAB allocations, sufficient smelter inventories and reduced operating rates at some RKEF lines are collectively limiting price recovery. The main variables to watch are the conversion of new RKAB allocations into actual shipments, the transmission of the revised HPM into transaction prices, inventory consumption at smelters and the recovery of water supplies in Morowali. If ore supply continues to increase while smelter consumption remains constrained, further declines in spot prices remain possible, particularly for medium- and high-grade saprolite.Oct 23, 2026 17:01 (GMT+8)

The model used some 24,400 copper assays from 140 holes, four geophysical datasets and geological models to estimate, on 25-metre blocks, where copper above a 0.5% threshold may occur, excluding mined-out areas and ground within 200 metres of existing holes. A 5,000-metre diamond and reverse-circulation program is underway, with logs and assays to refine the model. Milestones: maiden resource and PEA in Q4 2026, final metallurgy in Q1 2027, PFS in Q2 2027, production targeted for 2028. Pucobre may buy 30% by reimbursing 90% of eligible spending, minimum 10.2 million USD. A separate 5,500-metre program at Caballos starts in Q4 2026.6 hours ago

news.title: Korea Zinc Accelerates Germanium Expansion; KEMCO Targets Q4 Crude Germanium ProductionKorea Zinc recently said its subsidiary KEMCO began trial production of crude germanium products at Onsan, Ulsan, in August 2026. Mass production is scheduled to begin in Q4 2026, followed by commercial sales in Q1 2027. The company also plans to commence commercial production of 99.999%-pure germanium dioxide in H2 2027, significantly ahead of its original 2028 target. Korea Zinc also plans to expand its germanium production capacity through the Project Crucible integrated smelting complex in the US. Construction remains scheduled for 2027–2029, with completion and commissioning targeted for the end of 2029. The facility is expected to produce 13 strategic metals, including copper, lead, zinc, germanium, gallium and antimony. The accelerated KEMCO project, combined with the planned US facility, will further expand Korea Zinc’s role in germanium supply chains outside China.7 hours ago

The DFS is based on 5.5% Li2O spodumene concentrate from the Leia and Luke orebodies only. Metallurgical testwork confirmed a recovery of 75.7%, and the DFS model uses 74%.
